3. The contrary case of the defendants in brief is such that the suit is not maintainable and there is no. cause of action to file the suit which is barred by limitation and barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 and also barred by the principle of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence. The further case of the defendants is such that the plaintiffs are not entitled to challenge the legality and propriety of the order of termination of their service and it is not correct that nobody other than the Managing Director could terminate the service of the plaintiffs. In fact; the concerned authority in accordance with law terminated the plaintiffs and they were sacked because of their illegal strike and the Trade Union activities. In violation of the Service Rules as well as conduct rules of Bank the plaintiffs illegally took part in the strike inspire of giving them caution and remained absent for days together in the name of strike and the appropriate authority in accordance with law passed the order of termination which is an order termination simplicitor and not motivated or punitive. 

 15. I have come-across that the learned trial Court in deciding the issue No.2 i.e. on point of defects of parties opined that all the parties interested in the subject matter of the suit inasmuch as have impleaded as party in the suit there is no defect of party as alleged from the side of the defendants. On the point of limitation i.e. issue No.3 it was the observation of the Court that in view of the plaint and the evidence on record it is found that the suit has been instituted within time from the date of cause of action and accordingly this issue is decided in favour of the plaintiffs. As regard the issue Nos.1 and 4 i.e. maintainability of the suit in its present form under the ambit of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 it is concurrently observed by both the Courts that the suit is maintainable and the Civil Court have got every legal authority and jurisdiction to try the suit and that it was not barred by any law and in this regard the learned counsel on behalf of the petitioners referred two decisions of our Apex Court reported in 48 DLR (AD) 63 and 29 DLR (SC) 39.
